record.paper_title: The Critical Beta-splitting Random Tree II: Overview and Open Problems
record.original_question: Consider the fringe process given by the local weak limit of DTCS(n) from a random leaf. Study the scaling limit of its branchpoints after rescaling, in the point-process sense suggested by the paper.

evidence.quote: It is intuitively clear that there is a scaling limit of the discrete fringe process itself, the limit being representable as a point process of branchpoint positions.
Open Problem 17 Study that rescaled process.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let DTCS(n) denote the discrete-time critical beta-splitting tree on n leaves, defined recursively as follows. Start with a single clade of n leaves. A clade containing m ≥ 2 leaves is split into two sub-clades of sizes i and m−i (1 ≤ i ≤ m−1) with probability

  q(m,i) = (1/Z_m) · 1/(i(m−i)),  where Z_m = sum_{j=1}^{m−1} 1/(j(m−j)),

and splitting continues independently within each resulting sub-clade until every clade is a single leaf. The resulting rooted binary tree carries an integer "height" on each internal node equal to the number of ancestral splits separating the node from the root.

Pick a leaf v uniformly at random from DTCS(n) and consider the rooted, marked subtree visible from v along its ancestral spine: as n → ∞, the joint law of the spine of v together with the sequence of subtrees branching off the spine has a local weak limit, the fringe process. In this fringe process the ancestors of v form an infinite path on which "branchpoints" occur at certain integer heights, and at each branchpoint a sibling subtree is attached.

Represent the fringe process as a point process on ℝ_{≥0} (or on a suitable mark space) whose points are the heights of the branchpoints (decorated by the corresponding sibling subtree). Identify the appropriate rescaling of the height coordinate (and of the attached subtrees) under which this point process of branchpoint positions converges in distribution, and describe the resulting limit point process explicitly.
artifact.status_search_result: A subsequent work (arXiv:2412.09655) gives an explicit description of the limit fringe distribution of the critical beta-splitting tree relative to a random leaf, but it is not clear from public sources whether the rescaled point process of branchpoint positions in the fringe process has been fully analyzed and its scaling limit identified. No published resolution of this specific scaling-limit problem was found.
